question.problem:
Change the order of integration in the double integral 
${\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{4-x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14154008/assets/69bff6ba843a7d93cc9c60ec0adfe5986d4eea78beeca8806ec487c64f32310a.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 4,\,0\le y\le 4-x\}.
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
x=1
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
y=4-x\,⟹\,x=4-y.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 3,\,1\le x\le 4-y\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14154008/assets/47bc45edcaaa73ec6fb6010aa6d6fe35c77219b234d7f2b7210f12cec55e500d.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{4-x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{4-y}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
